title: India achieves 1,000-km quantum-secure communication milestone in three years: Jitendra Singh
key_facts: Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Saturday 10 Oct 2026 that India has reached a quantum-secure communication milestone of 1,000 kilometres within three years.
The article gives the target as 2,000 kilometres over eight years.
He spoke at the 121st Annual Session of the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry in New Delhi.
He said progress under the National Quantum Mission shows growing capability in areas critical to national security and strategic autonomy.
He urged industry to join research projects from the start and said private-sector research spending must rise.
The article does not say which technology, which links or which locations the 1,000 kilometres covers.
Singh also cited India's bioeconomy growth from about $10 billion in 2014 to nearly $196 billion, with a $300 billion target for 2030.
quote_evidence: New Delhi, Oct 10 (KNS): India has achieved a quantum-secure communication milestone of 1,000 kilometres within three years against an eight-year target of 2,000 kilometres, Union Minister of State for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Saturday, highlighting the country's progress in strategic technologies and calling for greater private-sector participation in research and innovation.

The Minister said the progress under the National Quantum Mission demonstrated India's growing capabilities in frontier technologies, particularly in areas critical to national security and strategic autonomy.
He urged industry leaders to become involved in research projects from their inception rather than waiting until technologies reached the final stages of development.
why_it_matters_hint: India says it is ahead of its quantum-secure communication schedule, which matters to government and security users, but the claim is a minister's and has no technical detail.
event_date: 10 Oct 2026 (speech); the milestone itself has no date in the article
